open_obligations: Check that the 2^(3q) factor keeps estimators efficient only for constant width q.
Check whether the soundness theorem rules out obfuscation as Buhl et al. define it.
Note the guarantee is average-case, which Brown-Cohen et al. list as a limitation.
in.other_title: Theorem 6.1 soundness: efficient estimator caps a dishonest prover's payoff
in.rationale: Buhl et al. list as open whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscation and whether its debaters can be built in polynomial time. Theorem 6.1 (soundness) gives, for every prover, an estimator among circuits of size O(q 2^(3q) n d^2 / eta^2) with oracle access to the prover that caps a dishonest prover's payoff, and stresses that stability is needed only for completeness; the size bound is exponential in width q, so polynomial size needs q constant.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscated arguments and how large the honest estimator must be

text: Among desired properties of improved debate protocols, the authors list as an open question whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscated arguments. They also note that lower complexity of reaching equilibrium makes equilibrium models more likely to be findable by stochastic gradient descent, and that for prover-estimator debate it is unclear whether the debaters can be constructed with polynomial-time algorithms.
title: Open: does prover-estimator debate avoid obfuscation, and are its debaters poly-time?
